iut_type: End Product (IDEAL Corporation device, Nordic S132-based SoftDevice), registration detail page shows a different SoftDevice version (S140) than what the customer specified
customer_question: On the registration site's detail page, the Included Design is described as 'S140 xxxx' -- but what we actually used, as stated in our quotation request, is S132-based Controller Stack and Host Stack. Tracing the S140 QDID/DN's link does show an S132-based module listed as a subset, so I don't think it's wrong, but is this just how it works?
question_variants: Why would a registration reference a different (parent) QDID than the one the customer actually specified?
Does this kind of substitution affect the registration's validity or accuracy?
actual_issue: The customer noticed their registration's displayed 'Included Design' referenced a different SoftDevice version (S140) than the one they had actually specified in their quotation request (S132), and wanted confirmation this was correct rather than a registration error.
plain_english_explanation: Since the registration system update effective July 1, 2024 (referred to internally as 'QPRD v3'), a structural change took effect: the new system can still reference QDIDs created under the prior system, but it can no longer reference legacy Subset IDs directly. Since the customer's specified S132 Link Layer and Host Stack were themselves registered as Subset IDs (subsets of the broader S140 registration), they could not be referenced directly under the current system -- so the registration instead referenced the original parent QDID that those Subset IDs were derived from (the S140-labeled registration), which is why the registration detail page displays 'S140 xxxx' rather than 'S132.' This is correct and not an error: tracing the S140 QDID/DN's links does show the S132-based module listed as a subset of it, confirming the underlying technical content the customer intended is still accurately represented -- the customer simply ended up seeing the broader parent registration's label rather than the specific subset label they were expecting, since the system can no longer reference the subset's own ID directly.
consultant_answer: You're right that this isn't an error. Since the registration system update on July 1, 2024, the new system can still reference QDIDs created under the old system, but it can no longer reference legacy Subset IDs directly. Your specified S132 Link Layer and Host Stack were themselves registered as Subset IDs of the broader S140 registration, so they couldn't be referenced directly anymore -- the registration instead references that original parent QDID (S140), which is why you see 'S140 xxxx' on the detail page. Tracing that QDID's links does show your S132-based module listed as a subset, confirming everything is accurately represented underneath -- you're just seeing the parent registration's label instead of the specific subset label you expected. Apologies for not explaining this proactively when we reviewed the Review page together.
decision_logic: When a customer's intended reference is itself registered as a legacy Subset ID, the post-July-2024 registration system substitutes the original parent QDID that the subset was derived from, since direct Subset ID references are no longer supported -- this produces a registration detail page showing the parent's label rather than the specific subset the customer specified, which is correct as long as the subset is still traceable from the parent QDID's links, and should be proactively explained to the customer rather than left for them to notice and question later.
final_recommendation: When a customer's specified reference turns out to be a legacy Subset ID requiring substitution with its parent QDID, proactively explain this substitution and what the customer will see on the registration detail page during the Review page confirmation step, rather than waiting for the customer to notice the discrepancy themselves and ask.
risk_if_done_wrong: Without proactive explanation, a customer noticing their registration shows a different SoftDevice version label than what they specified could reasonably suspect a registration error, creating unnecessary concern and follow-up communication that a brief upfront explanation would have avoided.
